text: The blood gas analysis reveals respiratory acidosis with hypoxemia, while the CBC is normal; this pattern suggests a primary ventilation issue rather than an infectious cause like Tuberculosis. Given the newborn status, was there any prenatal history of maternal infection or complications such as prematurity? REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray.

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood gas results indicate respiratory acidosis with hypoxemia, and the normal CBC makes sepsis less likely. Since you were born prematurely at 33 weeks, could you describe the character of your breathing distress, such as whether you are grunting or have flaring nostrils? REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of grunting, intercostal and subcostal retractions, and peripheral cyanosis in a 33-week premature infant with respiratory acidosis strongly suggests significant alveolar collapse or surfactant deficiency. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray.
